title: good defaults smart prefills
rule: Prefill with good defaults and smart values the user can accept or edit.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Getting Input — Good Defaults and Smart Prefills (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia); NN/g — A Checklist for Designing Mobile Input Fields

pass_when: Known defaults, history, or frequent values are prefilled and editable.
fail_when: User retypes a known default/history/frequent value with no prefill.
overview: Prefill editable defaults from known, historical, or frequent values.
apply_when: Fields with known defaults, history, or frequent prior values.
not_when: First-time fields with no reliable default or history to offer.
agent_hint: Prefill known defaults or frequent values and keep them editable.
description: Prefill with good defaults and smart values the user can accept or edit. Pass when known defaults, history, or frequent values appear prefilled and remain editable; fail when the user must retype a known default, history, or frequent value with no prefill. Defaults should speed completion, not lock the user into an uneditable guess they cannot change.
